headline: Weekend Brief: US equity futures steady as oil tops $90 on US-Iran tensions ahead of Leading Index data and key Big Tech earnings
raw_text:
- Escalation in the US-Iran conflict, including fresh strikes and disruptions to the Strait of Hormuz and Caspian Pipeline, pushed crude (@CL) above $90 a barrel and drove diesel prices higher, stoking inflation concerns
- US stock futures traded little changed after Wall Street’s losing week despite rising energy costs and renewed inflation worries
- Last week’s pullback in semiconductor and AI-linked names, including leveraged chip trades, related ETFs, and memory plays, intensified doubts about the durability of the AI rally and Magnificent Seven leadership
- Alphabet (GOOGL) and Intel (INTC) earnings later this week are viewed as key tests for the AI trade and the ability of Big Tech to continue carrying the broader market
- Energy producers stand to benefit from the oil price spike even as higher input costs and risk repricing threaten to weigh on broader US equity indices
- Trading in Asian and European markets on Monday is expected to help set the tone for US tech and semiconductor futures
- Monday’s US macro calendar is light, with the Conference Board Leading Economic Index due at 10:00 AM ET
- Monday’s earnings slate includes reports from AGNC Investment (AGNC), Crown Holdings (CCK), Domino’s Pizza (DPZ), Steel Dynamics (STLD), and Zions Bancorporation (ZION)
- A heavier Big Tech earnings calendar later in the week will test the ongoing rotation out of AI momentum names and interact with bond markets’ pricing of a prolonged inflation fight, heightening rate sensitivity across assets
